subject: art-design
title: Comparing Artists: Methodology
welcome_lead: Pair, compare, and articulate — A-Level contextual writing in practice.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: methodology for comparing artists in personal study.

concepts.def: A-Level extended written and visual study of artists and themes.
Setting two artists or works side by side to test ideas.
Close reading of formal qualities — line, colour, composition.
Reading the artwork through historical, social, political frames.
Referencing sources accurately (Harvard style commonly used).
A clear argued position the study sets out to test.

walkthroughs.body_html: A strong A-Level personal study opens with a thesis question, contextualises two or more artists, performs detailed visual analysis of named works, and concludes by linking research to candidate's own practice.

Combine visual analysis (formal qualities) with contextual analysis (when, why, for whom). For example, comparing Kara Walker and Lubaina Himid requires both formal close-reading and postcolonial framing.
Examiners reward an argued thesis, not a survey. Strong studies stake a position, support it with evidence, and engage with critics (Berger, Greenberg, hooks, Steyerl) by name and source.
